rationale: All four R5 round-1 asks are addressed at reviewed tip 0783a507. The bd-stderr content/render split now reaches the named cmd, next, approve, repair, release, and complete renderer families through the chain-preserving RenderBDError/bdRenderedError boundary; real-chain and per-family hostile fixtures preserve useful diagnostics while preventing raw ESC/CR/control bytes and forged standalone recovery lines. The net-new recovery-line chokepoint is the right containment: after per-line termsafe escaping, any line whose trimmed form begins with the reserved guard.RecoveryPrefix is strconv.Quote'd as data. Its false-positive cost is acceptable and deliberately conservative: an ordinary diagnostic beginning with the reserved prefix gains visible quotes, and a legitimate nested recovery line loses paste authority while retaining its text; outer trusted guard constructors remain the sole authority for executable recovery lines. Selector failures no longer interpolate caller-controlled selectors into command-shaped examples; hostile printable selectors remain diagnostic-only via %q, while candidate IDs pass through idrender. The residual warning is consistently renamed to WARN residual-artifact-dirt and the misleading stale fallback was removed. A scratch-targeted build succeeded; focused hostile tests in internal/next, internal/complete, and cmd/mindspec passed. A full go test ./... -short run completed all reported packages successfully but hit the global 10-minute timeout in unrelated internal/instruct TestRenderJSON_PanelState while waiting on an external bd subprocess, so that run is not represented as a full-suite pass. git diff --check passed and the dedicated scratch artifact was cleaned.

findings.title: Hostile bd stderr is contained across the requested renderer families
findings.detail: The named raw rendering sinks now route bd-derived chains through next.RenderBDError or bdRenderedError without severing errors.Is/errors.As. Hostile family fixtures cover state discovery, explicit-scope refusal through a real fake-bd chain, next claim-phase warnings, release sync, repair paths by inspection, approve warnings by inspection, complete lineage and phase-sync rendering, and command-tail guidance failures. Executed focused tests passed.
findings.evidence: cmd/mindspec/final_review_render_test.go; internal/next/scope_refusal_render_test.go; internal/complete/lineage_render_test.go; cmd/mindspec/next_render_test.go; cmd/mindspec/state.go; cmd/mindspec/next.go; cmd/mindspec/repair.go; cmd/mindspec/release.go; internal/approve/spec.go; internal/complete/complete.go

findings.title: Recovery-shaped stderr lines are safely demoted to quoted data
findings.detail: renderBDError escapes each line, then detects the reserved recovery prefix after whitespace normalization and applies strconv.Quote to the original line. This blocks clean printable-ASCII recovery forgery, including leading-space variants, while retaining the diagnostic text. The narrowly scoped false-positive behavior is appropriate at this hostile boundary.

findings.title: Printable-hostile selectors are absent from executable-shaped operands
findings.detail: The not-found and excluded messages now use operand-free `mindspec next` guidance, and ambiguity reports list actual idrender-gated candidates. Cases x;evil, $(evil), whitespace plus --help, --help, and backticks are pinned; the focused selector tests passed.

findings.title: Residual artifact warning follows the established WARN grammar
findings.detail: The only runtime spelling is WARN residual-artifact-dirt; the dotted snake_case spelling is gone, paths are escaped per entry, and the misleading knownResidualArtifactDirt fallback was deleted.
